newsitem.title: UK: China scatters ashes of Deng Xiaoping at sea.
newsitem.headline: China scatters ashes of Deng Xiaoping at sea.

text.p: The widow of China's late leader Deng Xiaoping scattered his ashes at sea on Sunday in accordance with his wishes, the official Xinhua news agency said.
It said Deng's ashes were escorted by senior Communist Party official Hu Jintao and other politicial leaders, Deng's widow Zhuo Lin and other members of his family.
Zhuo, 81, held a handful of the ashes "for quite a long time" before casting them into the waves along with flower petals, the agency said. They were scattered in a "simple yet solemn manner".

The report gave no hint of where off China's long coastline the ashes of Deng were scattered but said the waves might carry them to Hong Kong and Macao, two colonies whose scheduled return to Chinese rule count among Deng's most significant achievements.
"The waves would perhaps carry his ashes to the Pacific Ocean, the Indian Ocean and to the Atlantic Ocean, for he does not only belong to China, but also to the world," it added.
An aeroplane carrying the ashes and the mourners earlier circled Beijing slowly before heading for the sea, it said.

Hong Kong's TVB television station showed footage of a motorcade leaving Deng's home in a quiet alley behind the Forbidden City, home of China's emperors. Those inside the cars could be seen wearing white flowers, a symbol of mourning.
The motorcade was shown later leaving Zhongnanhai, the base for China's senior leaders, where soldiers with white flowers pinned to their uniforms saluted as the cars drove away
Deng died aged 92 of lung problems and complications from Parkinson's disease.
